# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code (or any agent) working in this repo.

## What this is

Debrup Banerjee's personal portfolio, deployed via GitHub Pages from the
`main` branch root. No Jekyll (`.nojekyll`), no server, no client framework.

## Critical rule: generated files

`index.html`, `assets/css/style.css`, and `assets/js/main.js` are **generated**
by `tools/build.js` from the source tree under `src/`. Each generated file
starts with a "Generated by tools/build.js" comment.

- **Never hand-edit these three files.** Edits will be silently overwritten
  the next time someone runs the build, and in the meantime the repo has two
  sources of truth that disagree.
- Edit under `src/` instead, then run `npm run build` (`node tools/build.js`)
  and commit both the `src/` change and the regenerated output. GitHub Pages
  serves exactly what's committed — it does not run the build.
- `404.html` is the one hand-authored page left; it's simple and rarely
  changes, so it wasn't folded into the generator.

## Source layout

- `src/data/site.js` — every piece of page copy (nav, hero, jobs, projects,
  skills, education, contact links, SEO meta, JSON-LD) as one plain object.
  Content changes (new job, new project, wording tweaks) belong here, not in
  a component file.
- `src/components/*.js` — one pure `(data) => htmlString` render function per
  section, plus `layout.js` for the outer `<head>`/`<html>` shell. Fields
  named `*Html` (e.g. `ledeHtml`, `impactHtml`) already contain inline markup
  and are inserted raw; every other field is treated as plain text and passed
  through `esc()` from `tools/lib/html.js`. Keep that convention when adding
  fields — don't put raw HTML entities (`&amp;`, `&#39;`) in a plain field or
  they'll be double-escaped.
- `src/styles/NN-name.css` — CSS split by section. The numeric prefix is the
  concatenation order (cascade order), not a priority ranking — keep new
  partials numbered consistently with their place in the visual flow.
- `src/scripts/NN-name.js` — one self-contained IIFE per behavior (theme
  toggle, mobile nav, header scroll, scrollspy/reveal, footer year).
  Concatenated in filename order into `assets/js/main.js`.
- `tools/build.js` — the whole build: renders HTML from data + components,
  concatenates the CSS partials, concatenates the JS partials. Zero
  dependencies, plain Node (`fs`/`path`), no npm install required.

## Workflow

```bash
npm run build   # regenerate index.html + assets/css/style.css + assets/js/main.js
npm run serve   # python3 -m http.server 8080, then open http://localhost:8080
```

After editing anything under `src/`, always run the build and check
`git status`/`git diff` on the generated files before committing — if the
diff looks unrelated to your change, something in the render path is wrong.

## Verifying a change didn't break content

There's no test suite. After a non-trivial edit to `src/`, sanity-check the
build:

```bash
for f in tools/build.js tools/lib/html.js src/data/site.js src/components/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done
node tools/build.js
git diff index.html assets/css/style.css assets/js/main.js   # eyeball it
```

A `git diff` on the generated files that's larger than your actual content
change usually means a data field's escaping convention (`Html` suffix vs
plain) is wrong somewhere.
